 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this claim petition against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Thimmarayappa S/o Rajappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 30.03.2023 the deceased Thimmarayappa was going towards his village Choodagondanahalli from Sampangere after attending mason work as a pillion rider in a Motor Cycle bearing No. KA05JG5087 ridden by his friend Ramalingappa on the left side of HosurMalur Road.

On the way at about 07.30 p.m in front of Krishnareddy Bricks Factory, Kodihalli Gate, Malur Taluk, Kolar District, Trailer Lorry bearing No.MH40CD2377 came in the same direction, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against ongoing Motor Cycle to its rear side and both the occupants of the Motor Cycle fell down on the road and Lorry ran over on Thimmarayappa and caused his death.

As on the date of accident the deceased was aged 30 years and was a Mason by profession and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m. The petitioners are entirely depending upon the income of the deceased and have put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.

The petitioners have spent Rs.50,000/
towards transportation of deadbody and funeral expenses of the deceased.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the daughter and petitioner No.3 is the father and petitioner No.4 is the (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 mother of the deceased.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said Lorry by its driver.
The respondent No.1 being the R.C. Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Lorry.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ with interest and costs.
03. In pursuance of service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased Thimmarayappa and denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased and also denied the alleged accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of lorry and admits that the driver of the offending lorry possesed valid and effective driving licence and lorry Rukmini N vs Cj Darcl Logistics Limited on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213006/
2 was insured with respondent No.2 and pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
05.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and contended that the driver of the trailer lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the (SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 time of accident and the owner of the lorry has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and Rules and they committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent is issued policy of insurance in favour of the respondent No.2 in respect of Trailer Lorry bearing No.MH40CD2377 and the liability of this respondent if any,
is limited to terms and conditions of the policy, subject to valid and effective driving licence and RC,
FC and Permit etc.,. and denied that the petitioners are the legal representatives and dependends on the earnings of the deceased and denied that the death of deceased is due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of offending lorry and denied that the death of the deceased was due to the injuries sutained in the alleged accident and further contended that as on the date of accident the rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA05JG5087 was negligent to who rode his Motor Cycle in a zigzag manner without noticing oncoming vehicles along the road abruptly stopped the Motor Cycle all of sudden in the middle of the road, due to which the rider lost control and made the deceased fell on the road due to skid and fall. The accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the rider of Motor Cycle who was riding his vehicle unmindfully along with pillion (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 rider both without wearing helmet and caused the accident and the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdiction Police have created false crime records and story about the manner and involvement of the lorry in the accident to get compensation and have lodged a false complaint against the insured vehicle.
The accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA05JG5087 who without having valid driving licence as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is highly exaggerated and excessive.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
06.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues: ISSUES 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependants of deceased Sri.Thimmarayappa S/o Rajappa?
02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Thimmarayappa S/o Rajappa died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 30.03.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, near Krishanareddy Bricks Factory, Kodihalli Gate, Malur Hosur Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar, due to negligent act of (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 driving of the Trailor Lorry bearing registration No.MH40CD2377 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

sentences.text: The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and one eye witness is examined as PW.2 and on behalf of the petitioners got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed their side evidence.
On the otherhand the respondents have not lead any evidence and no documents have been marked on behalf of the respondents and hence the respondents evidence is taken as nil.
08. I have heard the arguments advanced for the learned counsel of petitioners and the respondent No.2 counsel submits that its side arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.3036/2023  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1 & 2: In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in her chiefexamination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments.

Though she has been elaborately cross examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing has been brought on record to shows that deceased was not died in the road traffic accident and petitioners are not the legal heris and dependents of the deceased.

During the course of crossexamination by the respondent No.1 counsel she denied the suggestion that this accident occurred due to negligence of her husband and also denied the suggestion that the accident occurred when her husband was riding the motor cycle in high speed and the said accident occurred due to negligence of her husband and not due to the negligence of lorry driver and also denied the suggestion that there is no (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 negligence on part of lorry driver and also denied the suggestion that on the date of accident her husband was riding the motor cycle and also denied the suggestion that she and petitioners No.3 and 4 are living separately and also denied the suggestion that her husband was aged about more than 40 years at the time of accident and her husband was not doing mason work and not earning Rs.25,000/ and are not depending upon income of deceased.
11.

Further, PW.2 is eyewitness to the alleged accident was deposed about the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry by its driver and caused the accident and death of deceased in road traffic accident.

In the crossexamination by the learned counsel for the respondents he admits that "he was riding the motor cycle and he and deceased were going together for coolie work and he denied the suggestion that in order to reach home he was riding the motor cycle in high speed and also denied the suggestion that he and the deceased did not wore helmet and also denied the suggestion that if at all the deceased wore helmet he could have not sustained head injuries and Rukmini N vs Cj Darcl Logistics Limited on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213006/
4 denied the suggestion that he was proceeding in the center of road and this accident occurred due to his negligence and not due to the negligence of lorry driver (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 and also stated that he and the deceased were doing coolie work together in same place under mestri Nagaraj and denied the suggestion that this accident occurred due to his negligence without observing the vehicle movements".

sentences.text: Though these two witensses are elaborately crossexamined, but nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 14 documents as Ex.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Malur Police against driver of offending Lorry for rash and negligent driving and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against driver of offending Lorry.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report which discloses that both the vehicles are involved in the accident and Motor Cycle was heavily damaged.
Since the lorry was heavy goods vehicle, there is no visible damages found on the said vehicle and said accident occurred was not due to mechanical defects of the both vehicles.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Inquest panchanama of deceased Thimmarayappa.
This document also shows that the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.3 is father of the deceased.

Ex.P.6 is Post mortem report of deceased Thimmarayappa wherein it is stated that deceased died in road traffic accident and he was died due to (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 haemorrhage shock resulted due to head injury with polytrauma.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge sheet which was filed against driver of offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of Aadhaar card of the deceased Thimmarayappa.
Ex.P.9 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.10 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.11 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.3.
Ex.P.12 is the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.4 and Ex.P.13 is copy of Ration card pertaining to the family of deceased Thimmarayappa.

These Ex.P.8 to 13 documents clearly discloses that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is daughter, petitioner No.3 is father and petitioner No.4 is mother of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.
Ex.P.14 is copy of driving licence of PW.2 Ramalingappa who is the rider of the Motor Cycle as on the date of accident in which deceased was a pillion rider.
Therefore, it clearly discloses that the rider of the Motor Cycle had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident.

13. Therefore, on going through the entire evidence of PW.1 and 2 and Ex.P.1 to 14, it clearly establishes that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 No.2 is daughter, petitioner No.3 is father and petitioner No.4 is mother of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.

It is further established and proved that the deceased Thimmarayappa was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 30.03.2023, in front of Krishnareddy Bricks Factory, Kodihalli Gate, Malur Taluk, Kolar District due to rash and negligent driving of Trailer Lorry bearing No.MH40CD2377 by its driver.
Hence, the petitioners have proved Issues No.1 and 2.
Accordingly, this Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Thimmarayappa, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

PW.1 who is the wife of the deceased has stated that as on the date of alleged accident the deceased was aged about 30 years,
hale and healthy and working as Mason and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m and contributed entire income for the welfare of the family.

Petitioner No.2 is the daughther and petitioners No.3 and 4 are Rukmini N vs Cj Darcl Logistics Limited on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213006/
5 the parents of the deceased Thimmarayappa.

They have lost their earning member of the family,
love and affection of the (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 deceased and they have put to great mental agony and untold misery.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any school records and birth certificate of the deceased to show the date of birth of the deceased.
But as per police records at Ex.P.1 to 7 and as per Ex.P.8 attested copy of Aadhaar card of deceased, the date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 10.05.1992.
The alleged accident occurred on 30.03.2023 and in those documents the age of the deceased was mentioned as 30 years.
Therefore, in absence of evidence regarding the age of the deceased, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 30 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
16.

sentences.text: Though the petitioners have claimed that the deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m, but the petitioners have not produced any documents or material for the proof of (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 avocation and income of the deceased except oral evidence of PW.1 and 2.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding the avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, the notional income as per the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru

sentences.text: But in this case the accident is occurred in the year 2023, therefore Rs.500/ is added to the above income.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/ p.m and it is multiplied by 12.

Ex.P.8 to 12 copy of Aadhaar cards of petitioner No.1 to 4 and deceased Thimmarayappa and also Ex.P.13 Ration Card of the family members of Thimmarayappa it discloses that the petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is daughter, petitioners No.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased Thimmarayappa.

17. In this regard the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a decision reported in 2020 SCC ONLINE SC 28 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Birender, it has been held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased are entitled to make an application for compensation inview of Sec.166 (1)(c) of the Act.

It has further been held that, even major married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 representatives have right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representatives was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claims towards conventional heads only".
18.
In the instant case, nothing is placed before the tribunal that the petitioners are the earning members and not the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.
Since the dependants are 4 in numbers, therefore, as per law 1/4th of the income should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

19. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of Rukmini N vs Cj Darcl Logistics Limited on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213006/
6 estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 Sethi & Others case, the future prospects of the deceased is taking into consideration.

sentences.text: 20. Since the deceased was aged about 30 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the income to be Rs.22,400/.
Since there are 4 dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be Rs.16,800/.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.16,800/.
As the deceased was aged 30 years, a multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.

Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.34,27,200/
(Rs.16,800 x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.
21. The claimants No.1 being the wife and claimants No.3 and 4 are the parents they would each be entitled for Rs.48,000/ towards loss of consortium.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/4th of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this (SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;

sentences.text: Whatever contention taken by the respondent No.2 in its written statement has not at all proved by adducing evidence and no materials are placed on record to show that the rider and pillion rider of the Motor Cycle have contributed the accident and negligence on the part of Motor Cycle rider.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
(SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 24. Issue No.4:
In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.36,47,200/ (Rupees Thirty six lakhs forty seven thousand and two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 9% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.

The petitioner No.2 being the wife, petitioner No.2 being daughter, petitioners No.3 and 4 being parents were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50201515, in the award amount together with interest.

The petitioners No.1, 3 and 4 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through Epayment directly to their account by obtaining the bank (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since the petitioner No.2 is a minor, on deposit of the award amount, the entire share of the petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor petitioner No.2 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.2.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

The accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the rider of Motor Cycle who was riding his vehicle unmindfully along with pillion (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 rider both without wearing helmet and caused the accident and the petitioners in collusion with the jurisdiction Police have created false crime records and story about the manner and involvement of the lorry in the accident to get compensation and have lodged a false complaint against the insured vehicle.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my predecessor has framed the following Issues: ISSUES 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependants of deceased Sri.Thimmarayappa S/o Rajappa?
02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Thimmarayappa S/o Rajappa died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 30.03.2023 at about 07.30 p.m, near Krishanareddy Bricks Factory, Kodihalli Gate, Malur Hosur Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar, due to negligent act of (SCCH3) 7 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 driving of the Trailor Lorry bearing registration No.MH40CD2377 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
They have lost their earning member of the family,
love and affection of the (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 deceased and they have put to great mental agony and untold misery.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any school records and birth certificate of the deceased to show the date of birth of the deceased.
Though the petitioners have claimed that the deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m, but the petitioners have not produced any documents or material for the proof of (SCCH3) 14 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 avocation and income of the deceased except oral evidence of PW.1 and 2.
In the instant case, nothing is placed before the tribunal that the petitioners are the earning members and not the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.
Since the dependants are 4 in numbers, therefore, as per law 1/4th of the income should be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
19. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of Rukmini N vs Cj Darcl Logistics Limited on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119213006/
6 estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 Sethi & Others case, the future prospects of the deceased is taking into consideration.
20. Since the deceased was aged about 30 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the income to be Rs.22,400/.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.16,800/.
Whatever contention taken by the respondent No.2 in its written statement has not at all proved by adducing evidence and no materials are placed on record to show that the rider and pillion rider of the Motor Cycle have contributed the accident and negligence on the part of Motor Cycle rider.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, since insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Since there are 4 dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be Rs.16,800/.
As the deceased was aged 30 years, a multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.34,27,200/
(Rs.16,800 x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.
21. The claimants No.1 being the wife and claimants No.3 and 4 are the parents they would each be entitled for Rs.48,000/ towards loss of consortium.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,47,200/
with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.36,47,200/ (Rupees Thirty six lakhs forty seven thousand and two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 9% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
The petitioner No.2 being the wife, petitioner No.2 being daughter, petitioners No.3 and 4 being parents were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 50201515, in the award amount together with interest.
The petitioners No.1, 3 and 4 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through Epayment directly to their account by obtaining the bank (SCCH3) 20 M.V.C.No.3036/2023 account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since the petitioner No.2 is a minor, on deposit of the award amount, the entire share of the petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor petitioner No.2 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.2.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
